title: Defining and Calling
goal: In this lesson you will learn how to define a function with def and run it by calling its name with parentheses.
learn: Call a function by name with ()
Remember: defining does not run the body yet
idea: A function is a named block of code. You write it once with def, then run it by calling its name followed by (). Defining a function does not run it. The code inside only runs when you call the function. Everything inside the function must be indented under the def line.

lines: # Call it as many times as you want

changeOneLine: In the editor above, change the text inside print_stars from "*****" to "#####". Press Run. Both star lines should now show five hash marks.

practice.text: Finish say_hi() so it prints a short hello. Then call it twice.
practice.hint: Put a print() with a greeting inside say_hi — keep it indented. Defining the function does not run it; you must call say_hi() twice below.
practice.starterTip: Try print("Hi there!") inside the function, then add say_hi() on each blank line under the comment.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if say_hi is defined with def, prints something inside, and is called at least twice.

practice.text: Write print_banner() that prints a row of asterisks, a name, then asterisks again. Call it once.
practice.hint: The middle print() between the *** lines should show a name in quotes. After the function, call print_banner() once.
practice.starterTip: Change the empty print() to something like print("Team Python"), then add print_banner() on the line under the comment.
practice.starter:
def print_banner():
    print("***")
    print()
    print("***")

# Call print_banner
practice.gradingNote: Pass if print_banner is defined, prints stars above and below a name, and is called at least once.

quiz.question: When does the code inside a function actually run?

options.text: As soon as the def line is read
Only when the function is called by name
At the very end of the program automatically
Every time Python reads through the file

quiz.correct: Defining a function just saves it. The body runs only when you call it.
quiz.wrong: def stores the function. The code inside only runs when you call it.

quiz.question: Which line correctly starts a function named greet?
quiz.correct: Python uses def followed by the name and parentheses.
quiz.wrong: Use def, then the function name, then () and a colon.

quiz.question: What must be true about the lines inside a function?

options.text: They must be in ALL CAPS

quiz.correct: The body of a function must be indented under the def line.
quiz.wrong: Python uses indentation to show which lines belong inside the function.
